        - paragraph: In simple English
        - heading "Understand Cobweb Diagrams" [level=2]
        - paragraph: "A cobweb diagram visualises iteration of x_{n+1}=f(x_n). A useful rule is Cobweb iteration: x_{n+1}=f(x_n). You can learn Cobweb Diagrams by trying one small example instead of long theory."
        - paragraph: "Use Cobweb iteration: x_{n+1}=f(x_n). Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison."
        - paragraph: "In real life, population maps: Generations update one by one. Watch out: Jumping curve to curve without using y=x. Use the diagonal to feed output back as input."
        - complementary:
          - generic: Try this example
          - paragraph: State the core check for Cobweb Diagrams.
          - generic "Compare your answer"
      - text: CALCULUS
      - heading "Cobweb Diagrams" [level=1]
      - paragraph: "Objective: Visualise how iterates xₙ₊₁=f(xₙ) evolve using the cobweb diagram to study fixed points and stability."
      - article:
        - text: "Cobweb rule: Start at x₀ on the x-axis. Go vertically to y=f(x), then horizontally to y=x, and repeat."
        - text: The sequence xₙ₊₁=f(xₙ) follows the path.
      - complementary:
        - heading "Fixed points" [level=2]
        - paragraph: Fixed points satisfy f(x*)=x*, intersections of y=f(x) and y=x.
        - paragraph: "Stable: |f′(x*)| < 1"
        - paragraph: "Unstable: |f′(x*)| > 1"
